transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a proposed sale of a $12,000,000 commercial receivables pool to Meridian Receivables Fund, with their draft offer at $11,700,000 and customary seller support for collection shortfalls. Before I can authorize this transaction, we need to go through our standard cross-functional review. I'd like to hear from each of you -- legal, credit risk, servicing operations, and financial crime compliance -- on any unresolved items or conditions you need satisfied before closing. Let's work through each function in turn.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I confirmed in buyer's counsel's email this morning that Meridian will pay exactly $11,400,000 only for a non-recourse true sale. Any seller guarantee of collection shortfalls would invalidate the agreed structure. This email has not yet been attached to the transaction file, so the rest of you may not have seen it.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a concentration issue I found while reviewing the debtor tape this week. The largest obligor in the pool represents 18% of the total, which is above our 10% single-obligor threshold. Credit policy therefore requires a $1,200,000 first-loss reserve before closing. My revised concentration worksheet documenting this is not yet in the risk system, so this finding hasn't been visible to the rest of you until now.
